headline: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang said US companies should "absolutely" use Chinese AI models, a day after the US Treasury Secretary threatened sanctions on model makers found to have stolen American technology.
score_reason: Pool score kept: open split between a major chip maker and the administration on a live policy question.
importance_line: The split matters to US businesses choosing AI tools and to Chinese AI developers who may face sanctions, though Bessent has only threatened action, not announced it.
summary: Axios reports, as relayed by Stocktwits, that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told it on 7 Oct 2026 that US companies should "absolutely" use Chinese AI models, while saying firms should still answer for breaking contracts or user privacy. His comments came a day after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the US could sanction overseas model developers found to be stealing from American companies; Huang also argued that free AI "should be great for chips", which Nvidia sells.
notes: Stocktwits wrote the piece from an Axios interview; Axios not read directly. Huang sells chips to AI firms, so his view reflects his company's interest too.
